translations.answer: The thread provides a design→simulation→data collection→system identification→policy training→real deployment process, and publishes hardware/CAD, runtime/calibration, sim, identification, and motion training libraries together. Whether it can be directly reproduced depends on version and safety testing validation.
translations.applicability: Applicable to the minimum reproducible list for open-source humanoid robots.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal data cross-validation or independent reproduction is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Released full stack and provided blog/code.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Checked CAD, runtime, calibration, simulation, identification, and training for version binding.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Candidate mechanism is closed-loop versioned full stack, not isolated models.
translations.details.environments.0: Approximately $2,500 3D-printed humanoid; open-source soft hardware stack.
translations.details.limits.0: Not verified actual BOM, build time, and control performance.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The post claims it can be built, disassembled, repaired, simulated, and trained on real machine.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Low-cost humanoid projects often only open-source one layer, making it difficult to form a reproducible closed loop.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Low-cost/3D-printed structures still require load, fatigue, limit, and emergency stop validation.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Missing any layer would transfer system integration cost to the reproducer.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The post did not report specific faults.
translations.media_summaries.0: Screenshots show the LeRobot Humanoid paper/project cover and full-stack list, but no build error, control frequency, or real machine performance.
translations.source.locator: Root post and author's closed-loop reply
